s: A router's G0/0/0 must connect to a switch port that does not support auto-MDIX. Which cable is correct?
a: B. Router (MDI) to switch (MDI-X) are unlike devices, so straight-through. A crossover is for like devices; rollover is for the console; serial DCE is a WAN cable.

s:
SW3# show interfaces status | include Gi0/1
Gi0/1   Uplink-SW4   notconnect   1   auto   auto   10/100/1000BaseTX

SW4's Gi0/1 shows the same. The cable was just installed between the two switches, neither supports auto-MDIX, and both ports are configured no shutdown. What is the most likely cause?
a: B. Two switches are like devices and need a crossover when auto-MDIX is absent. A duplex mismatch (A) leaves the link up. VLAN (C) and STP (D) problems happen above Layer 1 on a link that is already up.

s: SW1 Gi0/1 shows Full-duplex, 100Mb/s. SW2 Gi0/1 shows Half-duplex, 100Mb/s and its late-collision counter is rising. Users report slow transfers, but pings work. What is the problem, which side was probably hard-coded, and how do you fix it?
a: Duplex mismatch. SW1 was probably hard-coded to 100/full; SW2 stayed on auto, detected 100 Mb/s, could not learn duplex and fell back to half. Late collisions on the half side are the signature. Fix: make both ends match — both auto, or both 100/full.

s: Which statements about a full-duplex Ethernet link are true?
a: A and C. Full duplex has separate transmit and receive paths, so there are no collisions and no need for CSMA/CD (B is wrong). Late collisions (D) indicate a fault. Hubs (E) are half duplex only.
o: CSMA/CD is used before every transmission
Both ends can send and receive at the same time
Late collisions are normal under heavy load

s: show ip interface brief shows GigabitEthernet0/0/1 unassigned YES unset administratively down down. What does this mean and what command fixes it?
a: Someone entered shutdown (and router interfaces start shut); there is also no IP address yet. Fix with interface g0/0/1, no shutdown, and an ip address if the interface is needed.

s: A switch port is set to auto. The connected device is hard-coded to 100 Mb/s, full duplex, with autonegotiation disabled. What speed and duplex will the switch port use?
a: B. Speed is sensed from the signal (100), but duplex cannot be learned, so the switch falls back to half duplex at 100 Mb/s — a duplex mismatch.

s: Two buildings on a campus are 2 km apart. Which fiber type and optic family would you choose for a 1 Gb/s link?
a: B. 2 km is beyond multimode reach for 1000BASE-SX (hundreds of metres); single-mode with LX/LH optics covers 5–10 km. Cat6a copper (C) is limited to 100 m. 10GBASE-SR (D) is multimode and also short reach.

s: DOM output for Gi1/1/2: Tx −5.0 dBm, Rx −27.0 dBm --. The far end's Tx is normal. Which are likely causes?
a: A and C. Very low Rx with a normal far-end Tx means light is lost on the path: dirty connectors and bends are the most common causes. Duplex, VLAN and STP are not optical problems.
o: Fiber bent too tightly or crushed

s: The far end transmits at −3 dBm and you receive −9 dBm. How many dB were lost, and roughly what fraction of the transmitted power arrived?
a: 6 dB lost (−3 − (−9) = 6). Every 3 dB halves the power, so 6 dB is half of half: about one quarter of the power arrived (exactly 10^−0.6 ≈ 0.25).

s: A serial interface shows up, line protocol is down. Which explanation fits best?
a: C. Up/down means Layer 1 is fine but Layer 2 is failing, classically an encapsulation mismatch (HDLC on one end, PPP on the other). An unplugged cable (A) gives down/down; shutdown (B) gives administratively down; IP subnet errors (D) do not change line protocol status.
o: Layer 1 works but a Layer 2 setting (such as encapsulation) does not match
The IP address is in the wrong subnet

s: A port shows full duplex at both ends, zero collisions, and a steadily rising CRC counter. The cable run measures 130 m. What is the most likely cause?
a: The cable exceeds the 100 m limit, so the signal is weak and corrupted, which shows up as CRC errors. Duplex is not the cause because both ends are full and collisions are zero.

s: Which counter in show interfaces records frames smaller than 64 bytes?
a: B. Runts are under 64 bytes; giants are over the maximum frame size; overrun and ignored count frames the receiver could not handle in time.

s: A port shows err-disabled after someone plugged in an unknown device. Which sequence restores it correctly?
a: C. err-disabled ports stay down until the cause is removed and the port is bounced. no shutdown alone (A) brings the port up only to be disabled again if the cause remains. Reloading (B) is disruptive and does not fix the cause.
o: Read the log to find the cause, remove the cause, then shutdown followed by no shutdown

s: On a 100BASE-TX link, which pins does a PC use to transmit?
a: A. MDI devices (PCs, routers) transmit on pins 1 and 2 and receive on 3 and 6; switches do the opposite.

s: A network assistant reviews show interfaces for Gi0/5 (full duplex, 1 Gb/s, CRC errors rising, zero collisions) and recommends: "Set duplex half on both sides to eliminate the errors." Is this a good recommendation?
a: No. Half duplex on a 1 Gb/s link would introduce collisions and is not even supported by most gigabit copper ports. With full duplex at both ends and zero collisions, rising CRC errors point to the physical path: test or replace the cable, check its length and route away from EMI, and confirm both ends are configured the same. Always check an assistant's recommendation against the evidence before applying it.

s: For 10.45.130.77/19, give the network address, broadcast address, usable range and number of usable hosts.
a: /19 → mask 255.255.224.0, block 32 in the 3rd octet. 130 falls in the block starting at 128 (128–159). Network 10.45.128.0, broadcast 10.45.159.255, usable 10.45.128.1 – 10.45.159.254, hosts 2^13 − 2 = 8,190.

s: How many usable host addresses does a /27 provide?
a: B. 32 addresses minus network and broadcast = 30. A counts the reserved addresses; C is /26; D is /28.

s: Which address can be assigned to a host in 172.16.20.0/22?
a: C. A /22 is a block of 4 in the 3rd octet: 172.16.20.0 – 172.16.23.255. A is the network address, B the broadcast, D is in the next block. 172.16.22.0 sits in the middle of the range, so it is a valid host.

s: Which addresses are RFC 1918 private?
a: A and D. 172.16.0.0/12 runs to 172.31.255.255, so A is private and B is public. C is just outside 192.168.0.0/16. E is shared CGNAT space (RFC 6598), not RFC 1918.

s: You must split 192.168.40.0/24 into at least 10 equal subnets, with as many hosts per subnet as possible. Which prefix do you use and how many hosts does each subnet get?
a: Borrow 4 bits (2^4 = 16 ≥ 10) → /28, mask 255.255.255.240, 14 hosts per subnet. Borrowing 3 bits would give only 8 subnets.

s: What is the longest prefix (smallest subnet) that supports 500 hosts?
a: B. /23 has 9 host bits: 2^9 − 2 = 510. /24 offers only 254.

s: A PC is configured as 192.168.1.130, mask 255.255.255.128, gateway 192.168.1.1. It can reach local hosts but nothing on other networks. What is wrong?
a: The host's subnet is 192.168.1.128/25 (.129–.254), but the gateway 192.168.1.1 is in 192.168.1.0/25. The gateway is outside the host's subnet, so the host cannot reach it. Fix: use the router address in .128/25 (for example 192.168.1.129), or re-address the host.

s: G0/0/0 on R1 is 10.10.16.1/21. When you enter ip address 10.10.20.1 255.255.255.0 on G0/0/1, IOS returns % 10.10.20.0 overlaps with GigabitEthernet0/0/0. Explain why.
a: A /21 is a block of 8 in the 3rd octet: 10.10.16.0 – 10.10.23.255. 10.10.20.0/24 lies inside it, so the two interfaces would be in overlapping subnets, which IOS forbids.

s: ipconfig on a Windows laptop shows 169.254.33.7, mask 255.255.0.0, and no default gateway. What does this tell you, and what is the next thing to check?
a: It is an APIPA address: the laptop asked for DHCP and got no reply. Check physical/Wi-Fi connectivity, the access VLAN, and the DHCP server or relay (ip helper-address, Chapter 14).

s: Using 192.168.100.0/24, allocate largest first for LANs of 60, 28 and 12 hosts and one point-to-point link. Which subnet does the 12-host LAN receive?
a: A. 60 → /26 at .0; 28 → /27 at .64; 12 → /28 at .96; the link → /30 at .112. B overlaps the /27; C is free but not the next aligned block in a largest-first plan; D is too small (6 hosts).

s: What is the most specific single summary for 172.20.32.0/24 through 172.20.39.0/24?
a: 172.20.32.0/21. Third octets 32–39 share their first 5 bits (00100xxx), so 16 + 5 = 21. Check: a /21 is a block of 8 in the 3rd octet and 32 is a multiple of 8.

s: Which prefix provides two usable addresses on a router-to-router link without wasting any?
a: C. A /31 has two addresses, both usable on point-to-point links (RFC 3021). /30 also gives 2 usable but wastes 2 addresses; /32 is a single address.

s: In VLAN 10, PC1 is 10.1.1.10/24 and PC2 is 10.1.1.200 with mask 255.255.255.128. Both use gateway 10.1.1.1. Which statement is true?
a: B. PC2's /25 subnet is 10.1.1.128/25, so its gateway 10.1.1.1 lies outside it and PC2 cannot reach remote networks. PC2 also treats PC1 (10.1.1.10) as remote, so PC2 → PC1 fails too. PC1 (/24) is configured correctly.
o: PC2 cannot reach remote networks because its gateway is outside its subnet

s: Convert 11011010 to decimal and 240 to binary.

A host configured as 10.20.30.64/26 cannot communicate. A network assistant says: "10.20.30.64 is the network address of its /26 subnet; assign 10.20.30.65 or higher instead." Is the recommendation correct?
a: Yes. A /26 is a block of 64 in the 4th octet, so 10.20.30.64 is the network address of 10.20.30.64/26 and cannot be used by a host. The usable range is .65 – .126. Before applying it, confirm the new address is free and that the gateway is in the same /26.

s: Write 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:ff00:0042:8329 in its shortest valid form.
a: 2001:db8::ff00:42:8329. Leading zeros dropped (0db8 → db8, 0042 → 42); the three zero hextets become ::.

s: Write 2001:db8:a::12 in full.
a: 2001:0db8:000a:0000:0000:0000:0000:0012. Four hextets are shown, so :: stands for four zero hextets.

s: A host's MAC is 00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E and the prefix is 2001:db8:acad:1::/64. What is its EUI-64 global address?
a: 001A2B | 3C4D5E → insert FFFE → 001a:2bff:fe3c:4d5e → flip the 7th bit of 00 → 02 → interface ID 021a:2bff:fe3c:4d5e → 2001:db8:acad:1:21a:2bff:fe3c:4d5e.

s: A router interface with MAC 0200.5e11.2233 builds its link-local address with EUI-64. Which address results?
a: B. 02 = 00000010; flipping the 7th bit gives 00000000 = 00, so the interface ID is 0000:5eff:fe11:2233 → fe80::5eff:fe11:2233. A forgot to flip; C inserted FFFE in the wrong place; D skipped FFFE.

s: How many /64 subnets fit in a /48? In a /56?
a: A /48 has 16 subnet bits before /64: 2^16 = 65,536. A /56 has 8: 2^8 = 256.

s: What type of address is fd12:3456:789a:1::10?
a: C. fd00::/8 is the used half of the unique local range fc00::/7.

s: All PCs in a new IPv6 VLAN show only fe80:: addresses and no default gateway. R1's interface has 2001:db8:acad:20::1/64 and is up/up. What is the most likely cause?
a: B. Without ipv6 unicast-routing R1 sends no RAs, so SLAAC hosts get neither a prefix nor a gateway; they keep only their link-local addresses. DHCPv4 (A) is unrelated; a duplex problem (D) would not produce this pattern.
o: The PCs need a DHCPv4 server
The switch port is in the wrong duplex

s: Which are valid IPv6 addresses?
a: B and D. B expands to 2001:db8:0:0:1:0:0:5 (eight hextets). D is valid: ::ffff:1 is six zero hextets followed by ffff and 1. A uses :: twice; C contains g; E has five digits in a hextet.

s: An administrator configures ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:50::1/80 on a LAN interface. Routers send RAs, but hosts never build a global address. Why?
a: SLAAC requires a /64 prefix so the host can add a 64-bit interface ID. A /80 leaves only 48 bits, so hosts ignore the prefix for autoconfiguration. Use /64.

s:
R2# show ipv6 interface brief
GigabitEthernet0/0/0   [up/up]
    FE80::1
    2001:DB8:ACAD:60::1
GigabitEthernet0/0/1   [up/up]
    FE80::2D0:97FF:FE44:5501

Hosts on G0/0/1 have no global addresses. What is missing?
a: G0/0/1 has only an automatic (EUI-64) link-local address — it was configured with ipv6 enable or nothing more. It needs a global address, for example ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:61::1/64, so its RAs carry a prefix.

s: Which multicast group does a Cisco router join only after ipv6 unicast-routing is entered?
a: B. ff02::2 is all-routers; IOS joins it when it acts as an IPv6 router. ff02::1 is joined by every IPv6 interface; ff02::5 is OSPFv3; D is a solicited-node group.

s: A host tests the tentative address 2001:db8:acad:10::abcd:1234 with DAD. To which solicited-node multicast address does it send the NS?
a: Take the last 24 bits (cd:1234) and append them to ff02::1:ff00:0/104 → ff02::1:ffcd:1234.

s: A router sends RAs with the M flag set to 1. Where do hosts get (a) their address and (b) their default gateway?
a: (a) From a stateful DHCPv6 server. (b) From the Router Advertisement — DHCPv6 never supplies a gateway.

s: Windows shows Default Gateway . . . : fe80::1%12. What does %12 mean?
a: It is the zone (scope) index: the interface number the link-local address belongs to. Every link uses fe80::/64, so the host must say which interface to use.

s: A network assistant recommends: "Use 2001:db8:acad:10::/120 on the Staff VLAN instead of /64 to avoid wasting addresses." Is this good advice?
a: No. LANs should use /64: SLAAC and EUI-64 need a 64-bit interface ID, and IPv6 has no address shortage to save. Longer prefixes are appropriate only on point-to-point links (/127) or loopbacks (/128).

s: Which hypervisor is Type 1?
a: C. ESXi runs directly on server hardware. VirtualBox, Workstation and Parallels are Type 2 and run on a host OS.

s: What does every virtual machine have that a container does not?
a: B. Each VM boots its own guest OS kernel; containers share the host's kernel. Both have IP and MAC addresses (A, C) and run applications (D).
o: Its own guest operating system kernel

s: Which are advantages of containers compared with VMs?
a: A and C. No guest OS means containers start quickly and are small. Isolation is weaker than VMs (B), they must use the host's kernel type (D), and they do need networking (E).
o: Can run a different OS kernel from the host

s: What is the role of a virtual switch inside a hypervisor?
a: It is a software Layer 2 switch that connects VMs to each other and to the host's physical NICs, places each VM's vNIC in a VLAN (port group), and tags frames with 802.1Q on trunk uplinks.

s: An ESXi host runs VMs in VLANs 10 and 20 through one uplink to SW1 Gi1/0/5. Which switch-port configuration fits?
a: B. VMs in two VLANs share one uplink, so it must be an 802.1Q trunk allowing both. A would carry only VLAN 10; C makes it a routed port; D is for IP phones.
o: switchport mode trunk and switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20

s: show mac address-table interface gi1/0/5 lists eight MAC addresses beginning 0050.56, in VLANs 10 and 20. What is most likely connected to Gi1/0/5?
a: A VMware ESXi host: 00:50:56 is the VMware OUI, and many MACs in several VLANs on one port is the signature of virtual machines behind a trunk.

s: After a new port group for VLAN 30 is created on an ESXi host, its VMs cannot reach their gateway. VMs in VLANs 10 and 20 work. show interfaces trunk on the switch shows Vlans allowed on trunk: 10,20. What is the fix?
a: Add VLAN 30 to the trunk: switchport trunk allowed vlan add 30 (and create VLAN 30 on the switch if it does not exist). Using add keeps 10 and 20; typing allowed vlan 30 alone would remove them.

s: A VM works on host ESX-A but loses its network every time it is live-migrated to ESX-B. What should you compare first?
a: Compare the trunk configuration on both hosts' switch ports, especially the allowed VLAN list. ESX-B's uplinks probably do not carry the VM's VLAN.

s: The switch logs %SW_MATM-4-MACFLAP_NOTIF for VM MAC addresses moving between Gi1/0/1 and Gi1/0/2, which connect to the same host. What is the likely cause?
a: The host's NIC teaming does not match the switch configuration — for example the host load-balances across two links while the switch treats them as independent ports (or the reverse). Make both sides agree: an LACP bundle on both, or independent links on both.

s: A Docker container runs nginx on port 80 and was started with -p 8080:80 on a host at 192.168.1.50. Which URL does a laptop on the LAN use?
a: C. Outside devices reach the container through the host's own address and the published host port 8080. 172.17.0.2 is private to the host's bridge.

s: A VirtualBox VM shows address 10.0.2.15 and your laptop cannot ping it. Which adapter mode is it using, and which mode would make it reachable from your home LAN?
a: It is in NAT mode (10.0.2.15 is VirtualBox's default NAT address), so the LAN cannot start connections to it. Bridged mode gives it an address on your home LAN.

s: Which is an example of network functions virtualization?
a: B. A router running as software on a general-purpose server or cloud is NFV. The others are physical hardware.
o: A Catalyst 8000V router running as a VM in the cloud

s: A network assistant reviewing a ticket says: "VM-Web in VLAN 10 cannot reach its gateway. Change the ESXi uplink port to switchport mode access and switchport access vlan 10." The same host also runs VM-Mgmt in VLAN 99. Is the advice correct?
a: No. An access port in VLAN 10 would fix VM-Web but cut off VM-Mgmt in VLAN 99. The correct check is whether VLAN 10 is allowed and active on the existing trunk (show interfaces trunk), and whether the VM's port group uses VLAN 10. Always test an assistant's suggestion against everything else using that port.

s: What is the default native VLAN on a Cisco 802.1Q trunk?
a: VLAN 1. Best practice is to change it to an unused VLAN on both ends.

s: Two connected switch ports are both left in dynamic auto mode. What is the result?
a: B. Both sides wait for the other to start negotiating, so no trunk forms and the link runs as an access link.

s:
Port        Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1       10,20,99
Port        Vlans allowed and active in management domain
Gi0/1       10,99

Hosts in VLAN 20 cannot reach the other switch. What is the most likely cause?
a: VLAN 20 is allowed but not active: it has not been created on this switch (or is suspended). Create it with vlan 20.

s: Gi0/1 is a trunk allowing VLANs 10 and 30. Which command adds VLAN 50 without removing the others?
a: B. A replaces the list with only VLAN 50, cutting off 10 and 30. C and D are not trunk commands.

s: Which ports are listed by show vlan brief?
a: A. Trunks are shown by show interfaces trunk; routed ports belong to no VLAN.

s: interface vlan 40 shows up/down. VLAN 40 exists. What is the most likely reason?
a: No port in VLAN 40 is up and forwarding (no access port connected, or VLAN 40 not allowed or forwarding on any trunk), so autostate keeps the SVI's line protocol down.

s: On a multilayer switch with SVIs for VLANs 10 and 30, hosts can ping their own gateway but not hosts in the other VLAN. What is missing?
a: ip routing. Each SVI works as a gateway, but without IP routing the switch will not forward packets between them.

s: Write the router-on-a-stick configuration on R1 G0/0/1 for VLAN 30 with gateway 10.10.30.1/24.
a: interface g0/0/1 → no shutdown; interface g0/0/1.30 → encapsulation dot1Q 30 → ip address 10.10.30.1 255.255.255.0. The switch port facing R1 must be a trunk allowing VLAN 30.

s: Which fields are part of the 802.1Q tag?
a: A and C. TPID (0x8100) and VID are tag fields; PCP and DEI are the others. TTL and checksum belong to IP; source port belongs to TCP/UDP.

s: SW1's management SVI (VLAN 99, 10.10.99.11) answers pings from hosts in VLAN 99 but not from VLAN 10. What is missing on SW1?
a: ip default-gateway 10.10.99.1. A Layer 2 switch is like a host: without a gateway it can answer only devices in its own subnet.

s: What does %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH tell you, and why does it matter?
a: The two ends of a trunk use different native VLANs. Untagged frames from one VLAN arrive in a different VLAN on the other side, causing leaks and broken connectivity. Set the same native VLAN on both ends.

s: Which command turns a Catalyst switch port into a Layer 3 routed port?
a: B. ip routing enables routing globally; A alone does not change a port. C does not exist; D creates an SVI.

s: VLAN 1500 belongs to which range?
a: C. 1006–4094 is the extended range.

s: An administrator deletes VLAN 30 by mistake. What happens to the access ports that were in VLAN 30?
a: The ports keep their switchport access vlan 30 setting but become inactive and pass no traffic until VLAN 30 is recreated.

s: A trunk allows VLANs 10, 30 and 99, and the printer VLAN 40 is missing. A network assistant suggests: "Run switchport trunk allowed vlan 40 on the trunk." Is this safe?
a: No. Without add, the command replaces the allowed list with only VLAN 40 and cuts off VLANs 10, 30 and 99. The safe command is switchport trunk allowed vlan add 40. Always check whether a suggested command replaces or appends.

s: Which LACP combination does not form a bundle?
a: C. Passive only answers LACP; with no active side, nobody starts negotiation.

s: One switch uses channel-group 1 mode active, the other channel-group 1 mode desirable. What happens?
a: No bundle. LACP and PAgP cannot negotiate with each other. Use the same protocol on both ends (LACP).

s:
Group  Port-channel  Protocol    Ports
------+-------------+-----------+-----------------------
2      Po2(SD)         LACP      Gi1/0/2(I)  Gi1/0/4(I)

What does this show, and what is the most likely cause?
a: Po2 is Layer 2 and down; both members are stand-alone (up, but not bundled). The far end is not negotiating LACP — for example both ends are passive, or the far end is not configured for EtherChannel at all.

s: show etherchannel summary shows Po1(SU) LACP Gi1/0/1(P) Gi1/0/3(s). What is wrong with Gi1/0/3?
a: Gi1/0/3 is suspended: its settings (allowed VLANs, native VLAN, speed or mode) differ from Gi1/0/1. Make it match, ideally by configuring interface port-channel 1.

s: Where is the IP address configured on a Layer 3 EtherChannel?
a: C. Members are routed ports with no address; the bundle has one IP.

s: Two hosts copy one large file across a 2 × 1 Gb/s EtherChannel. What is the most throughput that copy can get?
a: 1 Gb/s. All frames of one flow hash to the same member.

s: Why is src-dst-ip usually better than src-mac for a bundle between two Layer 3 devices?
a: Frames between two routers all carry the same pair of router MAC addresses, so a MAC-based hash sends everything down one member. IP addresses vary per conversation, so traffic spreads.

s: How many links can be active in one LACP EtherChannel?
a: C. Eight active; LACP can hold up to eight more in hot-standby.

s: Which settings must match on all members of a trunk EtherChannel?
a: B and C. Descriptions, port numbers and CDP do not affect bundling.

s: A technician enters channel-group 3 mode active on Gi1/0/21–22 and then no switchport on the port-channel, but show etherchannel summary still shows Po3(SD) with S. What went wrong?
a: The members were still Layer 2 when they joined, so Po3 was created as a Layer 2 port-channel. Remove the members from the group, apply no switchport to the members, then re-add them (and confirm no switchport on Po3).

s: show interfaces port-channel 1 reports BW 2000000 Kbit/sec. What does it tell you?
a: Two 1 Gb/s members are bundled: the port-channel's bandwidth is their sum (2 Gb/s). It does not mean one flow can reach 2 Gb/s.

s: Members go err-disabled with %PM-4-ERR_DISABLE: channel-misconfig. What is the likely configuration?
a: One side is set to on (static) while the other side is not bundling (or uses LACP/PAgP). The EtherChannel misconfiguration guard err-disables the ports to prevent a loop. Use LACP active on both sides, then bounce the ports.

s: Po2's members show (I). A network assistant recommends: "Change both sides to channel-group 2 mode on to force the bundle up." Is this the best fix?
a: No. on hides problems: it skips the checks that LACP performs and can create a loop if the far end is mis-cabled or misconfigured later. The correct fix is mode active on at least one side (best: both), with identical member settings.

s: Gi1/0/7 connects to an IP phone with a PC behind it. Data is VLAN 10 and voice is VLAN 20. Which two interface commands are essential besides switchport mode access?
a: switchport access vlan 10 and switchport voice vlan 20. (PortFast, BPDU guard and PoE auto are also normal.)

s: Does Gi1/0/7 from question 1 appear in show interfaces trunk? Why or why not?
a: No. The port is an access port with a voice VLAN (operational mode static access), so it is not listed as a trunk even though the phone's frames are tagged.

s: How do the phone's frames and the PC's frames differ on the link between the switch and the phone?
a: The phone tags its voice frames with VLAN 20 and CoS 5; the PC's frames are untagged and placed in access VLAN 10.

s: Which standard is PoE+ and how much power can the switch port supply?
a: B. 802.3af is the original 15.4 W PoE; 802.3bt is the higher-power standard; 802.3ad is link aggregation (LACP), not PoE.

s: show power inline shows Gi1/0/1 auto off 0.0 n/a. A PC is connected and working. Is there a fault?
a: No. off with no device class means no powered device was detected — a PC does not request PoE. Admin auto means the port would power a PD if one were connected.

s: A standalone AP broadcasts Staff-WiFi (VLAN 30) and Guest (VLAN 35); its management address is in VLAN 99. How should its switch port be configured?
a: As a trunk: native VLAN 99 (AP management, untagged) and allowed VLANs 30, 35 and 99, with spanning-tree portfast trunk and PoE.

s: A lightweight AP in local mode is managed by a WLC. Which switch-port configuration is typical, and why?
a: An access port in the AP management VLAN. Client traffic is carried inside the CAPWAP tunnel to the WLC, which maps SSIDs to VLANs, so the AP's port does not need the client VLANs.

s: Which UDP ports does CAPWAP use?
a: C. 5246 is CAPWAP control, 5247 is data. 67/68 are DHCP, 161/162 SNMP, 4789 is VXLAN.

s: Which protocols can tell an IP phone its voice VLAN?
a: A and C. CDP (Cisco phones) and LLDP-MED (multi-vendor) advertise the voice VLAN. DTP negotiates trunks; VTP shares VLAN lists; STP prevents loops.

s: A new IP phone receives an address in 10.10.10.0/24 (the data subnet) instead of 10.10.20.0/24. What is the most likely cause?
a: The port has no switchport voice vlan 20, or CDP/LLDP is disabled, so the phone never learns its voice VLAN and requests an address untagged in the data VLAN.

s: A new Wi-Fi 6 AP boots but only one radio comes up. The port is on an older switch. What should you check first?
a: PoE: the AP probably needs PoE+ (30 W) or more, but the port supplies only 802.3af (15.4 W) or the switch's budget is short. Check show power inline.

s: A hypervisor host uses LACP teaming on two NICs connected to Gi1/0/11–12 and carries VLANs 10, 30 and 99. Outline the switch configuration.
a: interface range gi1/0/11 - 12 → switchport mode trunk, switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,30,99 (plus native VLAN) → channel-group 11 mode active; then on interface port-channel 11 repeat the trunk settings and add spanning-tree portfast trunk.

s: Where should a building's IP security cameras be placed, and what else should protect them?
a: In a separate IoT/camera VLAN, usually PoE-powered, with ACLs (Chapter 20) allowing only the video recorder and management systems to reach them.

s: On a standalone AP's trunk port, Guest clients (VLAN 35) get no address while Staff clients work. A network assistant recommends: "Change the AP port to switchport access vlan 35." Is this a good fix?
a: No. An access port in VLAN 35 would carry only Guest traffic and break Staff-WiFi and the AP's management. The likely fault is VLAN 35 missing from the trunk's allowed list (or not created); fix it with switchport trunk allowed vlan add 35.

The documentation says "DSW1 Gi1/1/1 connects to CORE-2 Gi1/0/48". Is it correct?
a: No — the ports are swapped. The local port (DSW1's) is Gi1/0/48 and CORE-2's port is Gi1/1/1. Correct documentation: DSW1 Gi1/0/48 connects to CORE-2 Gi1/1/1.

s: Which protocol is the IEEE standard for neighbor discovery?
a: B. LLDP is IEEE 802.1AB; CDP is Cisco proprietary; DTP and VTP are not discovery protocols.

s: LLDP neighbors are empty on a Cisco switch connected to a non-Cisco switch that runs LLDP. What is the most likely missing command?
a: lldp run in global configuration. LLDP is often disabled by default on Cisco IOS.

s: R1 connects to DSW1, which connects to SW1. Will R1's show cdp neighbors list SW1? Why?
a: No. CDP advertisements are not forwarded, so each device sees only directly connected neighbors. You must log in to DSW1 to see SW1.

s: What are the default CDP advertisement timer and holdtime?
a: B. CDP sends every 60 seconds and keeps entries for 180 seconds. A matches LLDP.

s: Which pieces of information does show cdp neighbors detail provide that show cdp neighbors does not?
a: A and C. The summary already shows device ID, local interface, capability, platform and port ID; the detail view adds addresses, version, native VLAN and duplex.

s: On which interface should CDP be disabled first?
a: C. Advertising device details to the ISP or the Internet helps attackers and serves no purpose. Phone ports need CDP/LLDP for the voice VLAN; internal infrastructure links benefit from it.
o: A trunk to another campus switch
The router interface facing the ISP
An EtherChannel member between distribution switches

s: What does LLDP-MED add for an IP phone?
a: It lets the switch advertise the voice VLAN (and QoS) in a network-policy TLV, and lets the phone report its PoE requirements and inventory — the multi-vendor equivalent of what CDP does for Cisco phones.

s: CDP shows that DSW1 Gi1/0/2 connects to SW2 Gi0/1, but the documentation says SW2 Gi0/2. The network works and Gi0/1 is in the approved cabling plan. What do you change?
a: The documentation. The network is working and matches the approved design, so update the port table (and interface descriptions).

s: How would you verify the documented port of a printer that does not run CDP or LLDP?
a: Use show mac address-table interface <port> (and the ARP or DHCP table to match the printer's MAC to its IP), because the printer is invisible to CDP and LLDP.

s: You re-cable SW1 from DSW1 Gi1/0/1 to Gi1/0/5. For a few minutes show cdp neighbors shows SW1 on both ports. Why?
a: The old entry on Gi1/0/1 stays until its holdtime (180 s) expires; the new entry on Gi1/0/5 appears immediately. clear cdp table removes it sooner.

s: A network assistant analyses show cdp neighbors on DSW1 and reports: "R1 is connected to port G0/0/0 of DSW1." The line reads R1 Gig 1/0/24 ... ISR4331 Gig 0/0/0. Is the assistant right?
a: No. Gig 1/0/24 is DSW1's port (Local Intrfce) and Gig 0/0/0 is R1's port (Port ID). The correct reading is: DSW1 Gi1/0/24 connects to R1 G0/0/0. Check every assistant summary of neighbor output for this column swap.

s: In VLAN 1, SW-X has priority 32769 and MAC 0000.1111.2222; SW-Y has priority 28673 and MAC 00ff.ffff.ffff. Which is root, and why?
a: SW-Y. Priority is compared first and 28673 < 32769; the MAC address only breaks ties when priorities are equal.

s: With default settings, what bridge priority does show spanning-tree vlan 20 display?
a: B. 32768 + VLAN 20 = 32788 (the extended system ID).

s: Which is a valid command?
a: B. Priorities must be multiples of 4096 between 0 and 61440. 1000 is not a multiple; 65536 is too large; D has the wrong syntax.

s: Under Root ID, show spanning-tree vlan 30 prints "This bridge is the root". What else must be true of this switch's ports in VLAN 30?
a: It has no root port; every one of its ports in VLAN 30 that is up is a designated (forwarding) port.

s: What priority does spanning-tree vlan 10 root primary set if the current root uses the default priority?
a: 24576 (it sets 24576, or lower if needed to beat the existing root). With a default root at 32768 + VLAN, 24576 wins.

s: Which port roles forward traffic in a stable RSTP network? (Choose two.)
a: A and C. Alternate and backup ports discard; disabled ports do not participate.

s: How many port states does RSTP define, and what are they?
a: Three: discarding, learning, forwarding.

s: A switch can reach the root over a 100 Mb/s link directly, or over two 1 Gb/s links through another switch. Using short costs, which path wins?
a: Direct 100 Mb/s costs 19; two 1 Gb/s links cost 4 + 4 = 8. The path through the other switch wins (lower total cost).

s: SW2 has two 1 Gb/s links to the root bridge SW1: SW2 Gi0/1 connects to SW1 Gi0/2, and SW2 Gi0/2 connects to SW1 Gi0/1. Port priorities are default. Which SW2 port becomes the root port?
a: Costs and sender BID are equal (both links go to SW1), and port priority is 128 on both, so the lowest sender port number decides: the link to SW1 Gi0/1, which is SW2's Gi0/2. The neighbor's port ID matters, not your own.

s: What happens when a port with BPDU guard receives a BPDU, and what happens when a port with root guard receives a superior BPDU?
a: BPDU guard: the port is err-disabled immediately and stays down until bounced or recovered. Root guard: the port goes root-inconsistent (discarding) and recovers automatically when the superior BPDUs stop.

s: A technician enables spanning-tree portfast trunk on the trunk between two access switches to speed up convergence. Is this acceptable?
a: No. PortFast tells STP the port cannot form a loop; between two switches it can. Use PortFast only toward hosts (and host trunks such as hypervisors).

s: What problem does loop guard solve?
a: If BPDUs stop arriving on a root or alternate port (for example on a unidirectional link), normal STP would make that port designated and forwarding, creating a loop. Loop guard puts it in loop-inconsistent (blocked) state instead until BPDUs return.

s: %PM-4-ERR_DISABLE: bpduguard error detected on Gi1/0/7, putting Gi1/0/7 in err-disable state. What happened and how do you restore the port?
a: A BPDU arrived on Gi1/0/7, which has BPDU guard (usually because a switch was plugged in), so the port was err-disabled. Remove the device, then shutdown and no shutdown (or let errdisable recovery cause bpduguard restore it).

s: Where should root guard normally be configured?
a: B and D. Root guard protects the root position at the distribution layer by blocking superior BPDUs coming from below. It is not used on host ports (BPDU guard is) or on root ports.
o: Ports where an unauthorized root bridge could appear below the distribution layer

s: A user plugged a small unmanaged-looking switch into their desk port and it went err-disabled. A network assistant recommends: "Run no spanning-tree portfast bpduguard default so this does not happen again." Is this good advice?
a: No. That removes protection from every PortFast port and allows a user's switch to join the STP domain, risking loops and a rogue root. The correct response is to remove the switch (or provide a properly configured one), then recover the port.
